chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dowry (sadaq), whether it has a specific time [for payment]. He said, 'No.' Then he said, 'Indeed, the dowry of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was twelve ounces and a Nash, and the Nash is half an ounce, and the ounce is forty dirhams, so that is five hundred dirhams.'

key_terms.النَّشُّ: A specific weight unit, half an ounce

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the timing of paying the dowry and what was the Prophet's dowry amount?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the dowry (mahr) has no fixed temporal deadline for payment, emphasizing its status as a debt rather than a condition for the marriage contract's validity. By citing the Prophet’s dowry of twelve and a half ounces (500 dirhams), the hadith provides a concrete historical benchmark for valuation, reflecting the economic standards of the early Islamic period and offering jurists a tangible reference for assessing reasonable dowry amounts in Shia fiqh.
